reasons: Party roles are correct: Sparkling is the licensee/customer (Section 3(c) obligations run to Garman as licensor), and the edit expands Sparkling's rights while constraining Garman's — directionally right for our side.

The redline reaches the preferred position in full: affiliate/M&A successor carve-out without consent, express confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right, a reasonableness standard on other consents, and a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors.

The p0142 changed-character ratio (0.777) is advisory only — the original was a single short blanket-prohibition sentence, its operative language is preserved verbatim, and the added content is exactly what the rule requires, so the growth is inherent rather than over-drafting.
The p0033 conforming cross-reference to Section 20(d) is a minimal, coherent fix that prevents the licence covenant from re-imposing the prohibition the main edit removes.

The comment is accurate on what changed and why, cites the playbook position, offers the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on notice with reasonableness), and uses the required prefix and concise first-person-plural tone.
